title: picard_residue_homology_source_residue_comparison
statement:
Under the complete signature below, the explicit degree-one affine residue cycles modulo boundaries compute the derived residue fibre of any object represented by the strictly perfect complex; no geometric direct-image data are assumed.

Exact Lean statement:
theorem picard_residue_homology_source_residue_comparison
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{v},
      HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Y : Scheme.{v}) (U : Y.Opens), HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1}
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (W : Scheme.{v}) (E : schemeDerivedCategory W) (w : W)
    (U : W.Opens) (hwU : w ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (p : Ideal Γ(W, U)) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : p = RingHom.ker (W.evaluation U w hwU).hom)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hK : IsStrictlyPerfect W U K)
    (hE : Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{v}
      (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) :
    Nonempty (affineResidueCycleHomology W U p K ≃+
      derivedFiberCohomology W E 1 w)

source.place: Tags 01IB, 064K, 06YJ and 010V; affine projective retractions and module homology

proof.text: Let P be terminal sections of K. Applying the evaluation functor to each finite free retraction gives a retraction of P.X j from A^m. Retract.projective and ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat give flatness. Evaluation preserves zero objects, so the upper bound in hK bounds P. Apply the upstream CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat to obtain categorical K-flatness.

Transport the tilde/sections adjunction along the affine chart and over-site equivalence. Its counit is invertible on finite free sheaves. If i:M->F and r:F->M with r i=id, naturality shows that i followed by the inverse free counit followed by the image of r is an inverse counit at M. Apply this to each retraction in hK. Counit naturality assembles these components into a complex isomorphism sheafified P -> K. Compose Q of its inverse with hE. This is the elementary retract extension of the affine equivalence of Stacks 01IB, not an application of the finite-free reconstruction theorem to projective terms.

Apply affine_kFlat_residuePullback_model to P with the preceding K-flatness and representative, at z=(w,hwU). Affinity identifies the chart point prime with ker(W.evaluation U w hwU), and hp identifies this with p. The residue-field isomorphisms of the chart and open immersion intertwine the scalar maps. Their tensor maps and inverses therefore identify the model section complex with affineResidueTerm, naturally in each differential.

Exact sections on the one-point residue spectrum commute with degree-one homology. Use ShortComplex.moduleCatHomologyIso on the residue complex in degrees 0,1,2. Its module quotient has underlying additive quotient by affineResidueBoundaries, since the incoming differential squares to zero and its range in cycles is the comap range. The kernel description and surjectivity of affineResidueCycleClass give the same additive quotient, yielding the required equivalence.
